sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a decelerating growth curve: 64.2% in FY2021, 11.8% in FY2022, 0.1% in FY2023, then 16.4% and 10.6% in FY2024 and FY2025 [D218][D263][D311][D358][D406].
FY2017's operating loss of $3,485.6 million was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the IPO and the CEO award [F12][P74].
The FY2022 reversal, with the operating loss widening to $1,395.3 million, came from higher cost of revenue and operating expenses against only modest revenue growth [F17][P42].
Since then the operating loss has narrowed every year to $532.2 million in FY2025, a -9.0% margin versus a -32.4% window median [F20][F30][D555].
North America remains the largest geography at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D456][D458][D406].
Rest of world contributed 3.7pp on 17.0% growth and Europe 2.5pp on 14.1% growth [D499][D498][D524][D523].
Advertising revenue rose 5.8% to $5,186.1 million, driven by roughly 17% more impressions, partly offset by a roughly 10% lower cost per impression [S39][D537][P24].
Other revenue grew 62.9% to $745.4 million, now 12.6% of revenue, on higher subscription revenue from subscriber growth [S42][D543][D544][P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth, so the incremental operating margin was 44.8% [D423][D406][D429].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, against a -422.5% low in FY2017 and a -32.4% median [F30][D553][D555].
The 5.7pp improvement came mostly from R&D at 1.3pp, cost of revenue at 1.1pp and other lines at 3.3pp [D419][D432][D431][D433].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events and lower advertising, partly offset by higher headcount [P22].
R&D rose $101.9 million on product development and headcount, partly offset by $38.8 million of FY2024 restructuring charges [P23].
Net margin of -7.8% beat operating margin because other income of $68.9 million included $96.7 million of debt extinguishment gains [F50][X130][P18].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million and free cash flow of $437.2 million both exceeded the $460.5 million net loss in FY2025 [F80][F100][F40].
Free cash flow margin reached a window high of 7.4%, against a -4.1% median and a -167.5% low in FY2016 [D393][D561][D559].
Operating cash flow was lifted by $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $163.6 million of D&A added back to the net loss [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A, with spending mainly on leased facility improvements [F90][D392][D395][P10].
Net cash turned to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, down from $1,439.8 million of net cash in FY2021 [D399][D211].
That is -10.1% of revenue, in the 0th percentile against an internet peer median of 45.0% (n=5) [D400][D578][D579].
The FY2025 financing outflow of $848.1 million included $750.9 million of buybacks and $1.4 billion of note repurchases funded by new senior notes [F120][X156][P1][P2].
Buybacks were 171.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% to 1,694.6 million [D402][D425][X150].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2][D390].
Net cash has fallen for four straight years into net debt, and buybacks exceeded free cash flow in each of FY2023 to FY2025 [R3][R4][D399][D402].
The persistent losses and heavy stock compensation mean reported cash flow overstates economic earnings, and buybacks funded partly by debt add balance-sheet risk [R1][R2][R4].
Whether the operating margin holds above the FY2025 -9.0% level or slips back toward the -32.4% median, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D555].
Whether net cash returns above the FY2025 -$596.3 million or deepens further, given buybacks at 171.7% of free cash flow [D399][D402].
Whether stock-based compensation falls below the FY2025 17.1% of revenue, which would confirm the dilution trend is easing [D390][D425].
